locators.title: Proof. A power series \(f(x,y)\) can be presented in terms of its coefficients \(f(x,y)=\sum_{i,j=0}^{\infty} a_{ij}x^iy^j\). The unit axiom translates into the equations \(a_{i0}=a_{0j}=0\) for all \(i,j\). The commutativity condition can be stated as \(a_{ij}=a_{ji}\), while the associativity condition can also be presented as an equation the coefficients have to satisfy. Let \(L\) be the ring \(\mathbb{Z}[(a_{ij})_{i,j=0,\ldots,\infty}]/I\), where \(I\) is the ideal generated by these equations. The universal property of polynomial algebras guarantees that \(\mathrm{Hom}(L,R)\) is canonically equivalent to the set of formal group laws over \(R\). In particular, FGL \(\cong \mathrm{Spec}\,L\).
